name: Paperboy CPU PCB
notes: This board was published as one map that was really two. paperboy-video is the other half. The manual documents a CPU PCB and a Video PCB in one IC parts list, and their designators do not overlap — so nothing collided, nothing warned, and the merged map looked complete. Cell 5A on one is not cell 5A on the other, which makes a merged map actively misleading rather than merely incomplete. Found by asking, for every published board, whether its trusted rows sat under more than one figure heading naming a different PCB.
Only one printing is in the corpus, so nothing here is cross-checked against a second source.
Column-first designators, recorded in grid.transposed rather than inferred.
No component-location drawing has been read. The grid spacing is nominal.
conflicts: MAME's ROM map for this machine was NOT applied, and cannot be without someone looking at a board. This map's designators are column-first (2L), the convention Atari's later boards use, but MAME's map for the same machine is written row-first (L2). Reading one convention as the other transposes every position without saying so, so the tool refuses. MAME's 3 ROM positions are on the machine's ROM-map page, unattributed to a grid; none is on this map. Which convention the silkscreen actually carries is the open question, and it needs a physical board.
